scope: Offline static login session/cookie persistence and SDK request-construction comparison
evidence_type: ordinary DEX parsing + Android dexdump; not REA observation, not runtime capture

findings.claim: Both APKs expose a business AccountServiceImpl.getSessionKey bridge. SDK session key is returned first; null fallback queries the cookie key sessionid. New fallback domain is security.snssdk.com; old domain comes from account configuration.
findings.boundary: session_key is an SDK model/SP key; sessionid is a cookie key. Their runtime values and equality have NOT been observed.

findings.claim: Both SDKs persist account state in SharedPreferences com.bytedance.sdk.account_setting: session_key, session_sign, is_login, user_id and other account fields. Old h.j.ab loads, h.j.b saves; new impl.i.j loads, impl.i.n saves.
findings.boundary: Static persistence path only; did not inspect user files or prove installed account state.

findings.claim: Both SDK transport paths inspect Set-Cookie/sessionid and x-tt-token, x-tt-session-sign, x-tt-multi-sids; csrf cookie token is relayed as x-tt-passport-csrf-token. Old csrf SP is CsrfTokenManager_sp/csrf_token.
findings.boundary: Header names and parsing/transmission code, not live header values. TTNet/native cookie attachment behavior was not dynamically captured.

findings.claim: Successful business logout resets local account data and expires sid_tt, uid_tt, sessionid and sid_guard for .snssdk.com, then flushes cookies. Both also call TTTokenManager.clearToken.
findings.boundary: Old branch supports API<21 CookieSyncManager.sync, new branch directly flushes. Cookie clearing is not evidence of server-side revocation and does not assert all cookie domains/names are cleared.

findings.claim: Both SDKs construct POST /passport/mobile/sms_login/ using mobile and code transformed by StringUtils.encryptWithXor, mix_mode=1 and optional captcha. Old SDK additionally allows auth_opposite and extra map fields in this factory.
findings.boundary: SDK request construction only; no SMS was requested, no account was logged in. XOR transformation implementation was not expanded and no credentials were generated.

findings.claim: Old app user.a.a.a(String,String,String) creates user.a.a$31; its subscribe calls account.h.g.b(context) -> api.i.a(mobile,code,captcha,callback), an app business-to-SDK gateway. New SMS impl.c.g is confirmed at SDK construction level; the new UI/business caller was not fully traced.
findings.boundary: The UI event that selects this route, SDK api.i implementation dispatch and live request emission were not observed.

findings.claim: Old SMS success parser delegates l.b.r.b(JSONObject,JSONObject) -> h.c$a.b -> h.c$a.a -> account model. Old u.c.a(model,JSONObject,JSONObject) reads JSON session_key into model.h, with user_id/sec_user_id/new_user. Both transport paths separately collect Set-Cookie; exact live relationship between response session_key and cookie sessionid remains unknown. New SMS success parser kh1.d.i delegates impl.b$a.c -> wy7.d account model; that parser was not fully expanded.
findings.boundary: No claim that this is a complete response schema, nor that session fields are interchangeable. Existing candidate scans are leads rather than verified instruction boundaries.

findings.claim: Old app Douyin login code user.a.a$8/$13 uses AuthorizeFramework and aweme_v2 with app id literal 7828, user_info plus optional mobile, skip_auth_confirm, fanqie.follow scopes. New SDK impl.t.b constructs /passport/auth/login/ and delegates form construction to impl.b.b; that form was not fully expanded.
findings.boundary: Do not equate this Douyin authorization flow with SMS login, or claim every SDK route is used by a current UI.

limits: No APK execution, SMS request, login, account data read or library mutation.
Metadata candidate scans traverse all old/new DEX but code-unit scanning is heuristic and candidate-only; findings cite verified dexdump instructions.
No REA bridge calls were made by this worker; parent may add REA corroboration separately.
No inference that old and new services accept identical authenticated requests today solely from this static comparison.
